3) If a customer requests erasure, what constitutes proof? Will you provide an S3 object deletion timestamp + audit log id or a certificate of deletion for indexed artifacts?

Appreciate short bullets so we can include them in our vendor risk write-up.

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Short bullets below; attaching the retention matrix for quick reference.

- Default "kept by platform" items (hosted API, unless customer opts out):
  - request payload (prompt text + headers): kept for 45 days by default for debugging/abuse detection and quality metrics.
  - final model output (completed response): kept for 45 days by default.
  - streaming fragments (in-transit token buffers): not persisted as separate long-term objects in normal runs; platform buffers them in memory/ephemeral storage for the duration of the connection. We do snapshot streamed buffers to transient shards for resilience; those shards are pruned every 24 hours and not indexed for search.
  - KV cache: live-only in the serving layer and not indexed; we do not persist KV cache shards to durable object storage unless the customer has enabled session-replay backups (explicit opt-in).
  - embeddings and other derived vectors: treated as artifacts and will be retained if you explicitly call the embeddings endpoint or enable artifact capture; embeddings are not captured by default for text-generation calls.
  - metadata (confidence scores, token counts): kept alongside the request/response record and subject to the same retention window.

- How the API flags behave: 
  - store=false (API/SDK): prevents the request/response pair from being written to the default retention store. It is honored by both hosted and dedicated runtimes in normal operation.
  - ephemeral=true: marks session as non-indexable; ephemeral sessions still pass through transient buffers for streaming but are not archived. Use ephemeral=true when you want everything to be treated as in-memory-only for session lifetime.
  - note: store=false + ephemeral=true together provide the strongest guarantee in our hosted product. However, very short race windows can still create transient shards for live-in-flight resilience; these are pruned automatically (see auto-prune below).

- Transient vs durable storage and auto-prune: 
  - Auto-prune runs across our object stores on a rolling 24-hour cadence to remove transient shards, tombstones, and unindexed buffers. Durable indexed records are removed according to the configured retention TTL (default 45 days).
  - Deletion is logical + physical: we remove the index entry and then asynchronously remove underlying objects; physical deletion is reflected in our audit logs with an object-delete event id.

- Erasure and proof: 
  - For indexed artifacts: we provide a deletion confirmation record containing the index id(s), deletion timestamp, and object-delete event id(s) (S3 delete marker or equivalent).
  - For transient buffers: we provide a run id showing the auto-prune job that purged the transient shards; this is acceptable for routine compliance reviews but not always accompanied by a per-object S3 marker because transient buffers may never have been committed to durable storage.

Action items: I can get you a sample deletion record (S3 delete marker + audit id) and the retention matrix that maps API calls to default TTL. See attached.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alice — answers inline below.

A) Safety hooks & streaming: 
  - If a streaming fragment triggers a safety or moderation hook, we snapshot that fragment to an elevated investigation queue. By default those snapshots are retained for the standard TTL (45 days) to support incident review. 
  - store=false does not override mandatory security captures. We draw a distinction between customer-configurable archival and platform security telemetry — the latter is surfaced to customers as an incident record but cannot be suppressed by store flags. We do keep these records minimal and redact PII unless required for the investigation.

B) Private (VPC/on-prem) installs: 
  - Private deployments are separate: the default retention in Private is set at install time. Most customers we work with choose a 30–90 day TTL depending on their policy; it's configurable. For EU residency we routinely set 30 days by request and document it in the Private deployment runbook.

C) Deletion proof: 
  - For durable/indexed removals we will provide both the index deletion ids and the object-delete event markers (S3 delete markers or equivalent). Both items are included in the deletion confirmation package we send to customers.
